Waypoint.name: line_new_v5t92
Waypoint.Statement: Art is all—and only—what makes mortals gods.

Waypoint.name: line_new_2rc3h
Waypoint.Statement: Outlined hands on rock walls join a man of this time to men so distant they have forgotten their own history. Yet in that single instant, the artist’s hand reaches across ages and expands us. The hand of the artist is the path to immortality. It is immutable.

Waypoint.name: line_new_p9who
Waypoint.Statement: Whatever mortals know of the divine lives in their art. And all we know of the man in the cave is that his work is beautiful.

Waypoint.name: line_new_87lge
Waypoint.Statement: Long before that man pressed his hand to stone, races from distant stars came to this planet in their ships. Some were refugees, some exiles. All possessed knowledge so powerful they agreed, for the safety of this world, to abandon or sequester it lest humanity destroy their cradle as the celestials had destroyed their own.

Waypoint.name: line_new_prow1
Waypoint.Statement: So they built hidden cities and lived with the native peoples—who took them for gods.

Waypoint.name: line_new_uax64
Waypoint.Statement: Our island is one such refuge.

Waypoint.name: line_new_5du1t
Waypoint.Statement: In time, with gentle guidance, humanity rose to build civilizations. Some endured; others fell to catastrophe or to their own violence. Generations of such nations rose, perished, and were forgotten—leaving only ruins, memories of their might etched in stone.

Waypoint.name: line_new_nhph3
Waypoint.Statement: And while humankind forgot, we preserved their story here in the Library of Inanna.

Waypoint.name: line_new_usl4j
Waypoint.Statement: [gentle, instructive] We gave them rituals and symbols, teaching only what they needed to live together. Through trade they built great temples. And gathered in community to worship then returned to their own lands. Each season more gathered united by belief and trade. Each season they made the temples more grand. Then the priests lingered longer until the temples became their homes and they spent their lives writing.

Waypoint.name: line_new_pxebh
Waypoint.Statement: This encoding of the patterns of their lives worshiping their gods created shapes that have forever lived in their art.

Waypoint.name: line_new_0uauo
Waypoint.Statement: But as greater temples of knowledge bred greater power, and power returned them to savagery. Strong men displaced the priests and waged wars. What had been consecrated to gods became property of kings; temples became houses of prostitution. Offerings once made to sustain sacred order were given instead to raise monuments to men.

Waypoint.name: line_new_ude2i
Waypoint.Statement: And the women who served in the temples became property.

Waypoint.name: line_new_symdw
Waypoint.Statement: The temple servants of Eridu were driven into the mountains where the Jinn twisted their grief into vengeance. These became Lilith. Some of Ur heard the call of the Mother Goddess and crossed a continent to join us.

Waypoint.name: line_new_3xbg7
Waypoint.Statement: The temple servants of Egypt fled into the desert until Isis sent Osiris, their guardian, to find them and bring them to this island.

Waypoint.name: line_new_oxozo
Waypoint.Statement: Slowly the world’s temples collapsed, finally consumed in the era of the Great Burning. This fire devoured not only sanctuaries but the belief in the equality of men and women and the sacred art of love.

Waypoint.name: line_new_sxowj
Waypoint.Statement: As each temple fell, some of its servants were called home by their goddess to her temple on our island.

Waypoint.name: line_new_ps668
Waypoint.Statement: Thus the Garden of the Goddess became our sanctuary from those who could not bear to live peacefully in a world of magic. Sorcery was banished, and we became the last refuge of the old religion.

Waypoint.name: line_new_i3kfl
Waypoint.Statement: Beauty was profane.

Waypoint.name: line_new_8rap5
Waypoint.Statement: Where goes the impulse of the divine when beauty is profane? [pause] How does it rest? Sleep by the oak as a young girl? Live in the woods as an old man? Spit ochre on rock walls in torchlight?

Waypoint.name: line_new_cdjxz
Waypoint.Statement: Earth colors herald finality.

Waypoint.name: line_new_xidjw
Waypoint.Statement: It is ignorance because, when at peace—humble, awed, and wondering—they create beautiful works by seeing it in themselves.

Waypoint.name: line_new_31ql3
Waypoint.Statement: Belief in the one.

Waypoint.name: line_new_nir0d
Waypoint.Statement: One who seeks the divine lifts up beauty. To lift up self.

Waypoint.name: line_new_29ev6
Waypoint.Statement: We cannot retire from the world of men. We must tame them.

Waypoint.name: line_new_75ndl
Waypoint.Statement: The burning of the temples was not rebellion against us, but against humanity’s own divinity. They burn beauty and declare it the will of their gods. Then pray for it relentlessly and curse their gods for not providing means.

Waypoint.name: line_new_0pyvl
Waypoint.Statement: They create it and find it insubstantial. Inconstant.

Waypoint.name: line_new_xxlwo
Waypoint.Statement: Beauty fades.

Waypoint.name: line_new_rrq6x
Waypoint.Statement: Beauty mocks immortality.

Waypoint.name: line_new_whxtk
Waypoint.Statement: Love of beauty becomes hate of immortality. They sense that no matter what they build, they are insubstantial. They will die. Their names, their wealth, will peel away and become dust on the temple steps.

Waypoint.name: line_new_wfjwl
Waypoint.Statement: But the temples—like the ancient caves—will endure. Forgotten, lost, misunderstood, yet eternal.

Waypoint.name: line_new_qbk43
Waypoint.Statement: Waiting for those who spend their brief lives searching for something unknown yet knowable for a breath.

Waypoint.name: line_new_lmrg4
Waypoint.Statement: The temples were raised not by spoils of war but by trade in spice. Columns, spires, and gardens of stone are all built from sweet smoke. Their desire for that sweetness is why we protect the mortals.

Waypoint.name: line_new_gllgr
Waypoint.Statement: They need us. And we desire them.

Waypoint.name: line_new_xk4uo
Waypoint.Statement: They are our incense.

Waypoint.name: line_new_7j3i7
Waypoint.Statement: We cannot make them want, nor want what they want. It is not for us to leave their fates unsigned but to witness.

Waypoint.name: line_new_usqyn
Waypoint.Statement: We keep the works they leave behind and discover the hidden thread of their longing—what elevates them.

Waypoint.name: line_new_42uu4
Waypoint.Statement: Then we guide them along that thread.

Waypoint.name: line_new_kbwd9
Waypoint.Statement: And if someday they attain what they most secretly desire, their wanting will cease, and we may return to our temples.

Waypoint.name: line_new_3fl42
Waypoint.Statement: Civilizations rise in their ruins. One ruin is the foundation of the next. Empires fall, but we remain.

Waypoint.name: line_new_5zpbb
Waypoint.Statement: Here in our library, we preserve not order but beauty, that mortals and immortals alike may evolve.

Waypoint.name: line_new_g48wz
Waypoint.Statement: We rise on the smoke of their sweet impermanence.

Waypoint.name: line_new_1wdd3
Waypoint.Statement: We are constant through the truth of their inconstancy.

Waypoint.name: line_new_b0z27
Waypoint.Statement: We are changed by every step they take toward the temple seeking comfort.

Waypoint.name: line_new_0klty
Waypoint.Statement: That is our gold, and the way of the Mother Goddess.

Waypoint.name: line_new_ysg87
Waypoint.Statement: It is her desire that you become her hand—for we too are our own art, painted upon the walls of smoky caves.

Waypoint.name: line_new_vhltu
Waypoint.Statement: Blessed be.
